SOS="503097,503105,503153,503156,503085,503102,503170,503178,503137,503180,503144,503107,503184,503095"
echo "### (b) credit: limit vs open order value, AR"
q -c "select trim(h.cust_no) cust, trim(c.cust_name) name, c.crdt_limit, round(sum(d.ord_qty*d.unit_price) filter (where trim(h.status) in ('O','I','H'))::numeric,0) open_orders, count(distinct h.order_no) filter (where trim(h.status) in ('O','I','H')) n_open from ord_hedr h join customer c on trim(c.cust_no)=trim(h.cust_no) join ord_detl d on d.order_no=h.order_no where trim(h.cust_no) in (select trim(cust_no) from ord_hedr where order_no in ($SOS)) group by 1,2,3 order by 1;"
q -c "select doc_type, trx_type, count(*), round(sum(amount)::numeric,0) total, min(doc_date)::date, max(doc_date)::date from arhist group by 1,2 order by 1,2;"
echo "### (c) vendor flags for vendors on trial lines/POs"
q -c "select trim(v.vend_no) vend, trim(v.po_name) name, trim(v.terms_code) terms, v.pay_hold, trim(v.iso_cert) iso, v.iso_cert_exp::date, left(trim(coalesce(v.po_notes,'')),110) po_notes from vendor v where trim(v.vend_no) in (select trim(vend_no) from ord_detl where order_no in ($SOS) union select trim(vend_no) from po_hedr where po_no in (81766,81793,81797)) and (v.pay_hold or v.iso_cert_exp < '2026-12-31' or trim(coalesce(v.po_notes,''))<>'' or trim(v.iso_cert) is null or trim(v.iso_cert)='') order by 1;"
echo "### (e) master address vs SO ack ship-to"
q -c "select trim(cust_no) cust, trim(cust_name) name, trim(cust_addr1) addr1, trim(cust_city) city, trim(cust_state) st, trim(cust_zip) zip, trim(cust_cntry) cntry, left(trim(coalesce(res_ship_addr,'')),40) res_ship from customer where trim(cust_no) in (select trim(cust_no) from ord_hedr where order_no in ($SOS)) order by 1;"
input.description: Check credit, AR history, vendor flags, and master addresses

content.text:
Short answer: no. The design handles the document diffs and the ERP-rule checks, but the data has about nine kinds of problem we haven't designed for yet. I checked this by reading all 31 documents and cross-checking the ERP. I haven't fetched the T&C links or read the mailbox. I installed nothing, because a throwaway stdlib extractor was enough.

## What's in the data

| # | Order | Issues found |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Meridian | The SO says Net 45, but the PO and master say Net 30. The SO says Ship Partials, but the PO and master say ship complete. The master wants date code ≤12 months, but supplier PO 81797 says 36 months. PO 81797 line 2 ($198k of Bourns parts) isn't on the SO. |
| 02 | Northstar | PO and SO match. The PO is unsigned. It cites clauses Q2/Q5/Q11 and NSA-SCM-001, which we can't read. Line 2 needs 720k and only 4.2k is on hand, with no inbound supply. |
| 03 | Quarry | The PO says credit card, but the SO says Net 30. The PO says FCA and the SO says EXW. The PO requires country of origin, ECCN and HTS on the ack, and the ack has none. It bans China origin without approval, yet lines 1, 3 and 5 are China-sourced. Line 1 has ECCN 5A991.b, so it needs export review. |
| 04 | Pinecrest (jpg) | PO and SO match. Line 3 was quoted from stock, but only 5 are on hand. The lead times on lines 1 and 2 are shorter than quoted. |
| 05 | Copperfield (**scan**) | Line 1 quantity is 45,000 on the PO and 49,000 on the SO. The freight account is 000158830 on the PO and 000158380 on the SO and master. Supplier supply arrives 11/26 against need dates of 9/7 and 9/10. Line 3's cost and vendor differ from PO 81766. |
| 06 | Cobalt (**scan SO**) | Line 3 price is 19.382 on the SO, but the PO and quote say 18.636. That's +4% against a 2% tolerance. The customer part number 05673-001-XTD isn't on the SO. |
| 07 | Crescent (xlsx) | The SO and PO say Net 30, but the master says credit card. Open orders are $44.7k against a $25k limit. |
| 08 | Sandstone (eml) | The email gives a new ship-to, but the SO has the old one. Open orders are $104k against a $75k limit. Vendor V1007's ISO cert expires 9/3. |
| 09 | Ospreyfield (**scan PO**) | Line 2 is 9014177/Molex on the PO and 9014171/Murata on the SO. The account has the YIELD flag and is over its limit ($67.9k vs $50k). Vendor V1074 is on pay hold and V1118's cert expired 8/12. |
| 10 | Norwood (docx) | The PO says partials are acceptable, but the master says none without written approval. The same MPN is on two lines. The vendor on line 1 is on pay hold. |
| 11 | Oakridge (German) | The SO says Net 30, but the PO (Vorkasse), the quote and the master all say prepay. The PO requires country of origin and ECCN on the ack, and the ack has neither. |
| 12 | Granite Peak (**scan SO**) | PO and SO match. Demand is 660k on one item with 28k inbound, and there's no quote to price against. |
| 13 | Hollowbrook | PO and SO match. The PO is unsigned. Line 2 supply is due 10/10 against a need date of 9/22. |
| 14 | Ironclad | Essentially clean. |

The two SO acks I thought were safe text (06 Cobalt, 12 Granite Peak) are scans, as are two of the POs (05, 09). Some of the sharpest issues sit in them.

## What the design doesn't cover yet

1. **Scans.** Text extraction silently returns nothing. Detect an empty text layer and route to vision plus OCR. For account numbers and part numbers, read twice and escalate any disagreement with the image crop. The freight-account digit swap is exactly where OCR errors and real mismatches look alike.
2. **Our supplier POs as a check target.** Customer clauses and the vendor's `po_notes` need checking against our PO conditions. Meridian's 12-month date code against supplier PO 81797's 36 months is the example. PO 81766 also omits the vendor's "no substitutions" note.
3. **Supply timing and link recovery.** Compare inbound PO due dates, quote lead times (free text like `6-8 WKS` or `STOCK`) and est-ship dates. The ack sets est-ship equal to the requested date every time. `so_order_no` is also incomplete: Meridian's lines 1 and 2 are covered by an unlinked PO (81764), recoverable by item, quantity and cost.
4. **Aggregation.** Demand has to be summed across lines of the same item and across open orders. Credit needs open orders plus AR, and only matters for net-terms customers.
5. **Country of origin hierarchy.** The PO line's `src_cntry` should beat the item default. They conflict on several lines, for example MC3002P defaults to TW but its PO says CN. This is your $25k tariff story.
6. **Format traps.** The German PO writes `19.000` for 19,000 and `06.10.2026` for Oct 6. Part numbers like `064316` and `1N4749A,133` break if treated as numbers or put in a CSV. `del_date` is free text.
7. **Hidden content.** The T&C URLs live in link annotations, not the visible text. Two POs are unsigned.
8. **As-of date.** Cert expiry and quote validity should be judged on the order date, not today.
9. **Expected vs exceptional.** Almost every line has a supply shortfall. In a quote-to-order business, "needs sourcing" is normal, and "quoted STOCK but isn't" is the real exception. Without that split, reviewers drown.

## LLM fallbacks

Use them only to normalize and propose, never to flip a fail into a pass.

| Check | Deterministic first | LLM fallback? |
|---|---|---|
| Arithmetic, dates, numbers | Locale-aware parser, validated by qty×price=ext | No. Re-read the source instead. |
| Line matching | Normalized MPN + manufacturer, then assign by qty/price/date | Only on ties or lines with no MPN. A near-miss like 9014177 vs 9014171 is a flagged mismatch, not a match. |
| Manufacturer names | Mapping table (`Coilcraft`→`COIL`) | Propose new mappings, persist them after review. |
| Terms and Incoterms | Dictionary (`Vorkasse`, `Cash in Advance`, `FCA`) | Unseen phrasing, any language. |
| Lead-time text | Regex on `N-M WKS` | Odd strings. |
| Address compare | Normalize + fuzzy | Only the gray zone. |

Log every fallback decision with its citation.

## Scale

- **Volume isn't the problem.** The deterministic checks are cheap, the tables are small, and the 24–48 hour SLA means batch is fine.
- **ERP connections.** You're capped at 5 connections and 30s per query. Batch to one query per table per order and pool them.
- **LLM cost.** The T&C ledger is cached per customer revision. The per-order cost is one document extraction plus a few judgment calls. Use a cheaper model for classification and a stronger one for judgment.
- **Reliability.** Key runs on message ID + PO number + revision for idempotency, and retry with backoff on Graph and LLM limits.
- **ERP coupling.** Today's design is tied to this schema. Put the ERP behind an adapter before a second distributor.
- **Review fatigue.** This 14-order sample already averages several findings per order, so severity ranking and de-duplication matter more than throughput.

content.text:
Most of these would not benefit from a fallback LLM, and for some it would do harm. The risk is that an LLM tends to reconcile differences. In this data the differences are the findings: 9014177 vs 9014171, 000158830 vs 000158380, and 19.382 vs 18.636. A model that "helpfully" calls those the same part, account or price removes the finding.

## Rule of thumb

- **Use an LLM** when the problem is "I can't turn this into canonical form". The input is open-vocabulary, multilingual or noisy, and the output is a closed set or a cited span.
- **Don't use one** when the problem is "do these two values agree". Disagreement is the answer, and the fallback should be "unverifiable", never a guess.

## Verdict per check

| Check | Fallback LLM? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Detecting scans | No | Empty text layer means route to vision. Done in code. |
| Reading scanned docs | Not a fallback | This is a primary reader. Add a second independent reader (OCR vs vision) for digits and IDs and flag disagreement. |
| Number and date parsing | No | Detect locale, then use qty×price=ext to pick the right reading of Oakridge's `19.000` and `06.10.2026`. If it doesn't tie out, mark unverifiable. |
| Arithmetic, totals, inventory, credit, quote price, date compares | **Never** | Pure code. |
| Line matching | Mostly no | Match on MPN + manufacturer. Duplicate-MPN lines (Norwood, Granite Peak, Copperfield) are solved by assigning on qty/price/date. A near miss like Ospreyfield's is reported as a mismatch with the closest candidate attached. Maybe later, for lines with no MPN. |
| Manufacturer name → ERP code | **Yes, proposal-only** | The ERP has no manufacturer table (`COIL`, `SAMSNG`, `MXIC`, `MCHP`, `PHOENX`, `MEANWL`). Seed the mapping from the 14 acks, which print both. The LLM proposes unknown ones for review, and until approved the line is unverifiable. |
| Payment terms phrasing | **Yes, with audit** | The output is one of 6 term codes, which is small and checkable. Examples are `Vorkasse` and `Cash in Advance`. Scope it to the terms field: `Prepay & Add` on the SO is a freight term, not a payment term. |
| Incoterms, ship via, carrier and account | No | Regex plus an alias table (`Ex Works`→EXW). Account numbers never go through an LLM. |
| Address compare | No (v1) | Normalize and fuzzy-match. Sandstone's mismatch is a completely different street and city. |
| Customer name | No | Strip legal suffixes (GmbH, K.K.). |
| Lead-time text | No | The ERP strings (`6-8 WKS`, `12-16WK`, `STOCK`) are all regexable. Unparseable means unverifiable. Weeks from which date is a question for Aidan. |
| PO↔SO link and quote lookup | **No, and it would hurt** | Meridian lines 1 and 2 are recoverable exactly by item, quantity and cost. For the 8 SOs with no quote link, there are 3–16 old quotes per part, and none matches both quantity and price. I only tested exact matches. A fallback would pick a plausible old quote and "verify" against it. Report "no quote on file". |
| Country of origin and ECCN | No | A fixed hierarchy: PO line `src_cntry`, then item default, then unknown. |
| Ack boilerplate (AS6081, NCNR) | No | It's on all 14 acks, so use an allowlist. The model judges conflicts with customer clauses, such as Quarry's "Seller's own terms do not apply", as a primary judgment check. |

## What this means

Only three places benefit from a fallback:
- manufacturer mapping (proposal-only);
- terms and Incoterm phrasing (closed set, audited);
- gray-zone address and description matching, later.

The bigger robustness gains are second readers on scans, arithmetic tie-outs, and self-consistency on the LLM extraction steps. For clause extraction, run it twice with different chunk boundaries and send disagreements to unclassified.

## Guardrails if you add a fallback

1. Use ladder tiers: exact, then normalized, then fuzzy, then LLM proposal, then unverifiable.
2. The output must be a closed set or a cited source span.
3. Never use it on IDs, numbers or accounts.
4. Provenance marks an LLM-resolved value, and it can't produce a "pass" while the check's other inputs disagree.
5. Cache approved mappings so the fallback fires less over time.

Cost isn't the deciding factor, because these fire rarely. The deciding factor is correctness.

Yes, with three adjustments. The check isn't the agent reasoning freely about a clause. It's a small verifier that runs over the evidence.

## How it works

1. **The ledger row is parameterized.** For Quarry's clause 5 that's `prohibited_origin: [CN]`, `exception: prior written approval, per line`. The LLM only reads the clause into this form.
2. **A verifier in code decides each line.** The LLM isn't asked "does this violate?".
3. **There are three outcomes, not two:** violates, complies, or can't verify. For this clause, "violates" really means **needs approval**: hold the line and look for the written approval.

## Where the origin comes from

I hadn't looked at the lot tables before, and they change the evidence hierarchy I gave you. `lot_info.cnty_of_origin` is populated on all 1,955 lots, and it differs from the item default on **1,627 of them**. The item default is closer to a guess than a fact. The hierarchy should be:

1. The supplier PO line's `src_cntry`, for parts still to be bought.
2. The allocated lot's origin, for stock.
3. The item default, which is weak evidence and flagged as such.
4. Unknown.

Applied to Quarry:

| Line | Evidence | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 5 MC3002P | PO 81787 says CN, and past lots are CN | Needs approval, a firm hit |
| 1 INA02184-BLK | Item default CN, no lot or PO. It's also ECCN 5A991.b | Probable China origin, weak evidence. It needs an export review regardless. |
| 3 MMSZ10T1 | Item default says CN, the only lot says MX with balance 0 | Conflicting, so can't verify |
| 2, 4 016104 | Item default MX, lot says JP with only 460 in stock | Can't verify, since the supply for 4,100 is unknown |

Using the item default alone would have given wrong answers in both directions. It would have flagged line 3 incorrectly and passed lines 2 and 4 incorrectly.

## Three other points

- **Timing.** Often no supplier PO exists yet at order entry, so the first run is a prediction. Re-run the verifier when the supplier PO is placed, when a lot is allocated, and when receipt documents arrive.
- **Policy decisions in the parameters.** Whether "People's Republic of China" also covers Hong Kong or Macau is a business decision. Put the country list in the ledger row and have a human approve it. Don't leave it to the model.
- **Flow-down.** The same clause should also be checked against our supplier PO conditions. None of the supplier POs I read carry a no-China restriction.

The ledger works for this clause type once the evidence hierarchy is right. Not every clause type will be this clean. Anything without a verifier goes to unclassified for human review.

One thing to look into: `itm_inv` says 247,152 of MMSZ10T1 are on hand, but its only lot has a balance of 0. Those two inventory sources disagree, so the inventory check needs to say which one it trusts. `lot_info` also has a `tariff_amt` column, which is empty on these lots.

# Order validation agent: plan

Status: draft v1. This is the working plan for the Rama work trial. It records what we found in the data, what we decided, and what is still open. Update it as decisions change, and keep reasoning in `DECISIONS.md` as we go (the task asks for our thought process).

No credentials belong in this file or anywhere else in the repo. They live in `.env` (see section 11).

## 1. Goal and scope

Build an agent on top of the ERP with four parts: ERP read/write, Outlook integration, sales order (SO) and purchase order (PO) validation, and an ERP chatbot.

**Priority order**

1. SO/PO validation on the 14 customer orders and 3 supplier POs. This is the main workflow and the first milestone.
2. Outlook trigger: an order arrives by email, the agent validates it, then replies or flags someone.
3. Chatbot over the ERP, reusing the validator's ERP tools.
4. UI for progress (optional). Supplier ordering when stock is short is a stretch goal and out of scope for now.

**Scope decisions**

- For the trial orders the SO already exists in the ERP, so the agent validates and does not create SOs.
- The demo will send an unseen order. We do not know whether its SO will exist. The check runner therefore supports two modes: SO present, and PO only. Every check declares the inputs it needs and returns `unverifiable` when one is missing. This is an open question (section 10).
- Provider for the LLM is not fixed. The only model key in the task doc is for OpenAI. All LLM calls go through one wrapper that reads provider and model from `.env`, and the model must support vision.

## 2. What the data told us

Verified by reading all 31 documents and cross-checking the ERP.

**The ERP** is Postgres, schema `worktrial`, 33 tables. It has no document storage (no blobs or attachments), so PDFs, emails and approvals exist only outside it. `shp_hedr` and `shp_detl` are empty.

**Documents.** 14 customer POs, 14 SO acknowledgements (acks), 3 supplier POs.

| Format | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Text PDF | 23 | Includes one German PO (`19.000` is 19,000, `0,45980` is 0.4598, dates are DD.MM.YYYY). |
| Scanned PDF | 4 | Folders 05 (PO), 09 (PO), 06 (ack), 12 (ack). Text extraction returns nothing. |
| jpg | 1 | A skewed photo of a printed PO (04). |
| xlsx | 1 | No shared-strings table. |
| docx | 1 | Folder 10. |
| eml | 1 | Quoted-printable body. |

T&C links live in PDF link annotations and are not in the visible text. Two POs (02, 13) have a blank "Authorized by" line.

**ERP traps we hit, which the typed ERP tools must hide**

- Text columns are space padded, so always `trim()`. `trim()` fails on integer columns (`order_no`, `po_no`, `quote.quote_no`, `ord_detl.gen_quote_no`).
- `quo_detl.del_date` is free text (`6-8 WKS`, `12-16WK`, `STOCK`). `customer.res_ship_addr` is boolean.
- Part numbers can have leading zeros (`064316`) or commas (`1N4749A,133`). Always treat them as strings.
- The ERP uses manufacturer codes (`COIL`, `SAMSNG`, `MXIC`); documents use names. There is no manufacturer table.
- `customer` has 214 columns, `item` 170, `vendor` 145. We have only looked at the ones the task names. A column survey is a to-do (section 9).
- Item-default country of origin (COO) differs from the actual lot COO on 1,627 of 1,955 lots, so it is weak evidence.
- `itm_inv.qty_on_hnd` and `lot_hedr.bal_of_lot` can disagree (MMSZ10T1: 247,152 on hand vs a lot balance of 0).
- `po_detl.so_order_no` links PO lines to SO lines for only 63 of 4,008 lines. Some SO lines are covered by an unlinked PO that matches on item, quantity and cost (Meridian lines 1 and 2 via PO 81764).
- Order statuses are C, O, V, I, H. We assume O, I and H are open and H is hold. Not confirmed.
- All 14 acks carry the same boilerplate (AS6081 certified vendor, 1 year warranty, NCNR) and set Est Ship equal to the requested date.

Appendix A lists the issues we found per order. It seeds the eval answer key.

## 3. Architecture

```
sources -> ingest -> facts (with provenance) --+
ERP rows + requirements ledger ----------------+-> order bundle
                                               v
            checklist runner (code, fixed control flow)
              |- deterministic checks      (code)
              |- ledger verifiers          (one per clause type, code)
              '- judgment checks           (LLM + read-only tools, bounded)
                                               v
      rollup + policy (code) -> report + results table -> gated actions
```

**Principles**

1. The checklist drives control flow. The model never decides which checks run, so no item can be skipped.
2. Every value is a fact with provenance. Every finding cites the facts it compared.
3. Code compares and does arithmetic. The LLM extracts, normalizes to closed sets, and judges ambiguity.
4. When evidence is missing the status is `unverifiable`, never a guess.
5. ERP access goes through typed tools first, with read-only SQL as an escape hatch.
6. Writes (hold, email, results) happen only in a final gated stage, with a dry-run flag on by default.
7. Documents and emails are untrusted input. The extraction step has no tool access, and its output is validated against a schema.

## 4. Data models

- **Fact:** `id`, `value`, `raw`, `doc`, `location` (page, cell, line or bbox), `method` (text, ocr, vision, erp, email), `confidence`, `as_of`.
- **Requirement (ledger row):** `id`, `scope` (distributor, customer or order), `clause_type`, `params`, `quote` (verbatim), `source` (fact id or doc and location), `source_hash`, `status` (active or superseded), `reviewed`.
- **Finding:** `check_id`, `checklist_ref`, `status` (pass, fail, needs_approval, unverifiable, n/a), `severity`, `compared` (fact ids), `message`, `action`.
- **Order run:** `order`, `revision`, `as_of`, `findings`, `recommendation` (release, hold, needs approval), `state`.

**As-of date.** Cert expiry, quote validity and due dates are judged as of the order date, not the date the code runs.

## 5. Components

**`ingest/`** has one reader per format. Detect an empty text layer and route to vision plus OCR. For identifiers and numbers (accounts, part numbers, quantities, prices), read twice and flag any disagreement with the image crop. Detect locale and validate numbers by `qty x price = extended` and `sum = total`. Extract link annotations. Output is `facts.json` per document with header, lines, notes and links.

**`erp/`** has typed read functions that return facts and encapsulate the traps in section 2. They cover the order and lines, the customer master, the quote, linked and recovered PO lines, inventory and lots, vendors, AR and credit. Batch to one query per table per order. The same functions serve the chatbot.

**`ledger/`** has the closed clause taxonomy, the extractor and the verifiers.
- *Extraction.* Each source is split into units (by headings and numbering). Each unit gets exactly one label: a clause type with params and a verbatim quote, informational, or unclassified. A coverage check requires every unit to be labeled. Long T&Cs are chunked, with the heading path as context and a document-wide pre-pass for definitions. Results are cached per customer and `source_hash`. Run extraction twice with different chunk boundaries and send disagreements to unclassified.
- *Sources of requirements.* Standing: ERP flags (code, no LLM), `ord_notes` (dictionary first, LLM fallback), customer T&Cs. Per order: the PO's own notes and emails. Distributor: our checklist and own rules, such as CoC for unmarked SMT parts and prepay fees.
- *Verifiers.* One function per clause type. Unknown types return `unverifiable`.

**`checks/`** has a registry mapped to checklist item ids (section 6).

**`judge/`** has narrow LLM checks, each with its own prompt. Tools: `get_facts`, `read_source`, `get_requirements`, the ERP lookups, read-only SQL (SELECT only, read-only transaction, row limit), and `record_finding`, which rejects unknown fact ids.

**`report/`** does the rollup and policy, writes JSON and markdown per order, and writes a results table in `worktrial`. `set_order_hold` and `send_email` live here, behind the dry-run flag.

## 6. Check catalogue

Checklist references are to `data/Order_Processing_Checklist.docx`. All checks are code unless marked J (judgment).

**A. Document vs ERP and PO**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| A1 | Header: customer name (strip legal suffixes), PO number, dates, bill-to and ship-to, contacts (§2). |
| A2 | Commercial terms: payment terms, currency, Incoterm, ship via, carrier, account number, partial-shipment policy (§1, §2). |
| A3 | Lines: match on MPN + manufacturer, then compare qty, price, UoM, due date, customer P/N, description. MPN is exact (§2). Duplicate-MPN lines are assigned by qty, price and date. |
| A4 | Arithmetic: line extended, subtotal, total, tax. |
| A5 | Additions and omissions: ack content not requested (allowlist the standard boilerplate), PO content missing from the ack (notes, clauses). J for conflicts with customer clauses. |
| A6 | Ack PDF vs ERP rows (catches a stale or mis-exported ack). |

**B. Customer master and quote**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| B1 | SO terms vs master vs quote vs PO (§1). |
| B2 | Price and cost vs quote (apply the customer's tolerance, for example 2%), quote validity (`valid_days`), quote link recovery (§2). |
| B3 | Credit: limit vs open orders plus AR, for net terms only. Prepay fees (card 3.5%, wire $25) (§1). |
| B4 | Yield flag and required approvals (§3). |
| B5 | Ship account vs `shipinst`, partial instructions vs `no_partials` (§2). |
| B6 | Customer identity resolution: look-alike names exist (Sandstone Lighting C1143 vs Sandstone Electronics Manufacturing C1061, which has the Yield flag). |

**C. Supply**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| C1 | Stock: on hand minus committed, aggregated by item across lines and open orders. Reconcile `itm_inv` against lots and say which we trust (§4). |
| C2 | Inbound: linked and recovered PO lines, due date vs required date. |
| C3 | Lead time: Est Ship vs quoted lead time (regex on `N-M WKS`), and "quoted STOCK but not in stock" (§5). |
| C4 | Unrequested supply: PO lines for parts not on the SO (PO 81797 line 2, PO 81766 line 2). |
| C5 | Cost: SO unit cost vs PO unit cost vs quote cost, and margin. |

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| D1 | Country of origin with the hierarchy: PO line `src_cntry`, then allocated lot, then item default (weak), then unknown. Customer prohibitions need approval. The ack must state COO, ECCN and HTS per line when the customer requires it. Quantify China-origin value per order. |

| D3 | Date code, shelf life, AS5553/OCM, CoC and similar customer requirements vs our supplier PO conditions and vendor `po_notes`. |
| D4 | Vendor risk: `pay_hold`, ISO expiry as of order date, `po_notes`. |
| D5 | NCNR and T&C conflicts between the ack and the customer's terms. J. |

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| F1 | Unsigned PO, scan reads that disagree, locale mismatches. |
| F2 | SLA clock, such as "acknowledge within 48 hours". |
| F3 | Referenced but unread terms (links, clause codes like Q2/Q5/Q11, document ids). Always `unverifiable`. |
| F4 | Human-only checklist items (uploads, emailing inspection, test-report approval) are marked as such. |

## 7. LLM policy

Use an LLM only where the problem is "I cannot turn this into canonical form". Never use it to decide whether two identifiers or numbers agree, because disagreement is the finding.

| Step | LLM? |
|---|---|
| Document and clause extraction, email understanding | Primary. |
| Arithmetic, number/date parsing, comparisons, inventory, credit, quote price, origin hierarchy | Never. |
| Manufacturer name to code | Proposal only. Seed from the 14 acks, queue unknowns for review. |
| Payment-terms phrasing | Yes, closed set of 6 term codes, audited. Scope to the terms field. |
| Line matching | Only on ties or lines with no MPN. A near miss is reported as a mismatch with the closest candidate. |
| Incoterms, ship via, account numbers, address, customer name, lead-time text | Code only (regex, alias tables, fuzzy match). |
| Quote or PO link recovery | Code only. A guessed quote would "verify" against the wrong price. |

Fallback tiers: exact, normalized, fuzzy, LLM proposal, unverifiable. LLM output must be a closed set or a cited span. An LLM-resolved value is marked in provenance and cannot produce a pass while the check's other inputs disagree. Approved mappings are cached.

## 8. Build order

| M2 | Ingest all 14 POs and acks | All 14 produce `facts.json` and totals tie out. Scans, xlsx, docx, eml and the German PO all parse. |
| M3 | Families A and B | The eval shows recall on the doc-diff and master/quote/credit issues. |
| M4 | Family C | Supply, lead-time and link-recovery issues are caught. |
| M5 | Family D and the ledger verifiers | The origin, export and vendor findings match Appendix A. |
| M6 | Judgment checks and rollup | Each order has a recommendation and a readable summary. |
| M7 | Eval and mutation tests (section 9) | A scored report exists. |
| M8 | Outlook: poll the mailbox, classify, run, reply (to `test@tryrama.com`) | A dropped-in order is processed end to end. |
| M9 | Chatbot reusing the ERP tools | The two example questions in the task answer correctly. |

Perturb the extracted facts (change a quantity, swap two digits in an account number, swap terms, remove a line, change a price by 4%) and require detection. Degrade scan quality and check that disagreements are flagged.
- **Negative control:** Ironclad (14) is essentially clean. It should produce no failures.
- **ERP survey:** list the unexplored `customer`, `item` and `vendor` columns and the tables we have not inspected (`cust_itm`, `slsman`, `req_*`, `rfq_*`, `comm_due*`) for anything the checklist needs (tax exemption, credit application, MOQ, testing flags).
- **Consistency:** the validator and the chatbot share one definition of "open order" and "credit exposure".

## 10. Other problems to solve

Not yet in the catalogue.

1. **Revised POs.** The task says revisions are attached next to the original. Pick the latest, diff against the previous revision, record which revision was checked, and re-run on change. None of our sample folders has one, so check the mailbox.
2. **Email handling.** Classify incoming mail (new PO, revision, approval, question, noise), thread it to the order, handle multiple attachments, and keep approvals that arrive only by email. Match the mailbox copy of each PO against the folder file in case they differ.
3. **PO-only mode** if the SO does not exist (section 1).
4. **Approval workflow.** States: requested, granted or denied, attached, re-run. Know who approves what (Yield, price variance, restricted origin) and how the agent recognizes a grant.
5. **Customer and manager emails.** Draft the discrepancy email asking for a revised PO or written acceptance, and the approval request. Track the waiting state and the 24 to 48 hour clock.
6. **State machine and idempotency.** received, extracted, checked, awaiting customer, approved, released. Re-running must not duplicate holds or emails.
7. **Attachment storage.** The ERP has no document storage, so approvals and uploads need our own store and tables. This is also where a check result is "recorded".
8. **Units and order multiples.** UoM, minimum order quantity and multiples. A PO description includes "Min Qty:250".
9. **Tariff exposure and margin.** The task's $25k tariff story is a thin-margin problem. Report China-origin value and per-line margin, and flag margin shifts versus the quote. We do not have tariff rates, so this is exposure, not cost.
10. **Substitutions.** Vendor notes forbid substitutes without written approval. Compare SO item against what the supplier PO actually bought.
11. **Security.** Prompt injection from document text, fetching T&C links (they point to an external host), secrets in transcripts.
12. **Demo latency.** An unseen order is processed live. Parallelize calls, pre-warm the customer ledger cache, and keep a fast path.
13. **Generalization.** Avoid hard-coding to the 14 orders (the mutation tests help).
14. **Multi-tenant.** Put the ERP behind an adapter before a second distributor.
15. **Review fatigue.** Distinguish "needs sourcing" (normal) from "quoted STOCK but not in stock" (exception), and rank by severity.

## 11. Repo hygiene and deliverables

- `.env` holds DB, Graph and model credentials. Add `.env` and `task.md` (it contains credentials) to `.gitignore`. Commit `.env.example` with variable names only.
- AI transcripts are required in full and unedited, and they will contain credentials. Rotate or scrub before sharing.
- Keep `DECISIONS.md`, a README on how to run, and a `KNOWN_LIMITS.md` for the demo conversation (what falls short, what we would do next).

# Order validation agent: plan

Status: draft v1. This is the working plan for the Rama work trial. It records what we found in the data, what we decided, and what is still open. Update it as decisions change, and keep reasoning in `DECISIONS.md` as we go (the task asks for our thought process).

No credentials belong in this file or anywhere else in the repo. They live in `.env` (see section 11).

## 1. Goal and scope

Build an agent on top of the ERP with four parts: ERP read/write, Outlook integration, sales order (SO) and purchase order (PO) validation, and an ERP chatbot.

**Priority order**

1. SO/PO validation on the 14 customer orders and 3 supplier POs. This is the main workflow and the first milestone.
2. Outlook trigger: an order arrives by email, the agent validates it, then replies or flags someone.
3. Chatbot over the ERP, reusing the validator's ERP tools.
4. UI for progress (optional). Supplier ordering when stock is short is a stretch goal and out of scope for now.

**Scope decisions**

- For the trial orders the SO already exists in the ERP, so the agent validates and does not create SOs.
- The demo will send an unseen order. We do not know whether its SO will exist. The check runner therefore supports two modes: SO present, and PO only. Every check declares the inputs it needs and returns `unverifiable` when one is missing. This is an open question (section 10).
- Provider for the LLM is not fixed. The only model key in the task doc is for OpenAI. All LLM calls go through one wrapper that reads provider and model from `.env`, and the model must support vision.

## 2. What the data told us

Verified by reading all 31 documents and cross-checking the ERP.

**The ERP** is Postgres, schema `worktrial`, 33 tables. It has no document storage (no blobs or attachments), so PDFs, emails and approvals exist only outside it. `shp_hedr` and `shp_detl` are empty.

**Documents.** 14 customer POs, 14 SO acknowledgements (acks), 3 supplier POs.

| Format | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Text PDF | 23 | Includes one German PO (`19.000` is 19,000, `0,45980` is 0.4598, dates are DD.MM.YYYY). |
| Scanned PDF | 4 | Folders 05 (PO), 09 (PO), 06 (ack), 12 (ack). Text extraction returns nothing. |
| jpg | 1 | A skewed photo of a printed PO (04). |
| xlsx | 1 | No shared-strings table. |
| docx | 1 | Folder 10. |
| eml | 1 | Quoted-printable body. |

T&C links live in PDF link annotations and are not in the visible text. Two POs (02, 13) have a blank "Authorized by" line.

**ERP traps we hit, which the typed ERP tools must hide**

- Text columns are space padded, so always `trim()`. `trim()` fails on integer columns (`order_no`, `po_no`, `quote.quote_no`, `ord_detl.gen_quote_no`).
- `quo_detl.del_date` is free text (`6-8 WKS`, `12-16WK`, `STOCK`). `customer.res_ship_addr` is boolean.
- Part numbers can have leading zeros (`064316`) or commas (`1N4749A,133`). Always treat them as strings.
- The ERP uses manufacturer codes (`COIL`, `SAMSNG`, `MXIC`); documents use names. There is no manufacturer table.
- `customer` has 214 columns, `item` 170, `vendor` 145. We have only looked at the ones the task names. A column survey is a to-do (section 9).
- Item-default country of origin (COO) differs from the actual lot COO on 1,627 of 1,955 lots, so it is weak evidence.
- `itm_inv.qty_on_hnd` and `lot_hedr.bal_of_lot` can disagree (MMSZ10T1: 247,152 on hand vs a lot balance of 0).
- `po_detl.so_order_no` links PO lines to SO lines for only 63 of 4,008 lines. Some SO lines are covered by an unlinked PO that matches on item, quantity and cost (Meridian lines 1 and 2 via PO 81764).
- Order statuses are C, O, V, I, H. We assume O, I and H are open and H is hold. Not confirmed.
- All 14 acks carry the same boilerplate (AS6081 certified vendor, 1 year warranty, NCNR) and set Est Ship equal to the requested date.

Appendix A lists the issues we found per order. It seeds the eval answer key.

## 3. Architecture

```
sources -> ingest -> facts (with provenance) --+
ERP rows + requirements ledger ----------------+-> order bundle
                                               v
            checklist runner (code, fixed control flow)
              |- deterministic checks      (code)
              |- ledger verifiers          (one per clause type, code)
              '- judgment checks           (LLM + read-only tools, bounded)
                                               v
      rollup + policy (code) -> report + results table -> gated actions
```

**Principles**

1. The checklist drives control flow. The model never decides which checks run, so no item can be skipped.
2. Every value is a fact with provenance. Every finding cites the facts it compared.
3. Code compares and does arithmetic. The LLM extracts, normalizes to closed sets, and judges ambiguity.
4. When evidence is missing the status is `unverifiable`, never a guess.
5. ERP access goes through typed tools first, with read-only SQL as an escape hatch.
6. Writes (hold, email, results) happen only in a final gated stage, with a dry-run flag on by default.
7. Documents and emails are untrusted input. The extraction step has no tool access, and its output is validated against a schema.

## 4. Data models

- **Fact:** `id`, `value`, `raw`, `doc`, `location` (page, cell, line or bbox), `method` (text, ocr, vision, erp, email), `confidence`, `as_of`.
- **Requirement (ledger row):** `id`, `scope` (distributor, customer or order), `clause_type`, `params`, `quote` (verbatim), `source` (fact id or doc and location), `source_hash`, `status` (active or superseded), `reviewed`.
- **Finding:** `check_id`, `checklist_ref`, `status` (pass, fail, needs_approval, unverifiable, n/a), `severity`, `compared` (fact ids), `message`, `action`.
- **Order run:** `order`, `revision`, `as_of`, `findings`, `recommendation` (release, hold, needs approval), `state`.

**As-of date.** Cert expiry, quote validity and due dates are judged as of the order date, not the date the code runs.

## 5. Components

**`ingest/`** has one reader per format. Detect an empty text layer and route to vision plus OCR. For identifiers and numbers (accounts, part numbers, quantities, prices), read twice and flag any disagreement with the image crop. Detect locale and validate numbers by `qty x price = extended` and `sum = total`. Extract link annotations. Output is `facts.json` per document with header, lines, notes and links.

**`erp/`** has typed read functions that return facts and encapsulate the traps in section 2. They cover the order and lines, the customer master, the quote, linked and recovered PO lines, inventory and lots, vendors, AR and credit. Batch to one query per table per order. The same functions serve the chatbot.

**`ledger/`** has the closed clause taxonomy, the extractor and the verifiers.
- *Extraction.* Each source is split into units (by headings and numbering). Each unit gets exactly one label: a clause type with params and a verbatim quote, informational, or unclassified. A coverage check requires every unit to be labeled. Long T&Cs are chunked, with the heading path as context and a document-wide pre-pass for definitions. Results are cached per customer and `source_hash`. Run extraction twice with different chunk boundaries and send disagreements to unclassified.
- *Sources of requirements.* Standing: ERP flags (code, no LLM), `ord_notes` (dictionary first, LLM fallback), customer T&Cs. Per order: the PO's own notes and emails. Distributor: our checklist and own rules, such as CoC for unmarked SMT parts and prepay fees.
- *Verifiers.* One function per clause type. Unknown types return `unverifiable`.

**`checks/`** has a registry mapped to checklist item ids (section 6).

**`judge/`** has narrow LLM checks, each with its own prompt. Tools: `get_facts`, `read_source`, `get_requirements`, the ERP lookups, read-only SQL (SELECT only, read-only transaction, row limit), and `record_finding`, which rejects unknown fact ids.

**`report/`** does the rollup and policy, writes JSON and markdown per order, and writes a results table in `worktrial`. `set_order_hold` and `send_email` live here, behind the dry-run flag.

# Order validation agent: plan

Status: draft v1. This is the working plan for the Rama work trial. It records what we found in the data, what we decided, and what is still open. Update it as decisions change, and keep reasoning in `DECISIONS.md` as we go (the task asks for our thought process).

No credentials belong in this file or anywhere else in the repo. They live in `.env` (see section 11).

## 1. Goal and scope

Build an agent on top of the ERP with four parts: ERP read/write, Outlook integration, sales order (SO) and purchase order (PO) validation, and an ERP chatbot.

**Priority order**

1. SO/PO validation on the 14 customer orders and 3 supplier POs. This is the main workflow and the first milestone.
2. Outlook trigger: an order arrives by email, the agent validates it, then replies or flags someone.
3. Chatbot over the ERP, reusing the validator's ERP tools.
4. UI for progress (optional). Supplier ordering when stock is short is a stretch goal and out of scope for now.

**Scope decisions**

- For the trial orders the SO already exists in the ERP, so the agent validates and does not create SOs.
- The demo will send an unseen order. We do not know whether its SO will exist. The check runner therefore supports two modes: SO present, and PO only. Every check declares the inputs it needs and returns `unverifiable` when one is missing. This is an open question (section 10).
- Provider for the LLM is not fixed. The only model key in the task doc is for OpenAI. All LLM calls go through one wrapper that reads provider and model from `.env`, and the model must support vision.

## 2. What the data told us

Verified by reading all 31 documents and cross-checking the ERP.

**The ERP** is Postgres, schema `worktrial`, 33 tables. It has no document storage (no blobs or attachments), so PDFs, emails and approvals exist only outside it. `shp_hedr` and `shp_detl` are empty.

**Documents.** 14 customer POs, 14 SO acknowledgements (acks), 3 supplier POs.

| Format | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Text PDF | 23 | Includes one German PO (`19.000` is 19,000, `0,45980` is 0.4598, dates are DD.MM.YYYY). |
| Scanned PDF | 4 | Folders 05 (PO), 09 (PO), 06 (ack), 12 (ack). Text extraction returns nothing. |
| jpg | 1 | A skewed photo of a printed PO (04). |
| xlsx | 1 | No shared-strings table. |
| docx | 1 | Folder 10. |
| eml | 1 | Quoted-printable body. |

T&C links live in PDF link annotations and are not in the visible text. Two POs (02, 13) have a blank "Authorized by" line.

**ERP traps we hit, which the typed ERP tools must hide**

- Text columns are space padded, so always `trim()`. `trim()` fails on integer columns (`order_no`, `po_no`, `quote.quote_no`, `ord_detl.gen_quote_no`).
- `quo_detl.del_date` is free text (`6-8 WKS`, `12-16WK`, `STOCK`). `customer.res_ship_addr` is boolean.
- Part numbers can have leading zeros (`064316`) or commas (`1N4749A,133`). Always treat them as strings.
- The ERP uses manufacturer codes (`COIL`, `SAMSNG`, `MXIC`); documents use names. There is no manufacturer table.
- `customer` has 214 columns, `item` 170, `vendor` 145. We have only looked at the ones the task names. A column survey is a to-do (section 9).
- Item-default country of origin (COO) differs from the actual lot COO on 1,627 of 1,955 lots, so it is weak evidence.
- `itm_inv.qty_on_hnd` and `lot_hedr.bal_of_lot` can disagree (MMSZ10T1: 247,152 on hand vs a lot balance of 0).
- `po_detl.so_order_no` links PO lines to SO lines for only 63 of 4,008 lines. Some SO lines are covered by an unlinked PO that matches on item, quantity and cost (Meridian lines 1 and 2 via PO 81764).
- Order statuses are C, O, V, I, H. We assume O, I and H are open and H is hold. Not confirmed.
- All 14 acks carry the same boilerplate (AS6081 certified vendor, 1 year warranty, NCNR) and set Est Ship equal to the requested date.

Appendix A lists the issues we found per order. It seeds the eval answer key.

## 3. Architecture

```
sources -> ingest -> facts (with provenance) --+
ERP rows + requirements ledger ----------------+-> order bundle
                                               v
            checklist runner (code, fixed control flow)
              |- deterministic checks      (code)
              |- ledger verifiers          (one per clause type, code)
              '- judgment checks           (LLM + read-only tools, bounded)
                                               v
      rollup + policy (code) -> report + results table -> gated actions
```

**Principles**

1. The checklist drives control flow. The model never decides which checks run, so no item can be skipped.
2. Every value is a fact with provenance. Every finding cites the facts it compared.
3. Code compares and does arithmetic. The LLM extracts, normalizes to closed sets, and judges ambiguity.
4. When evidence is missing the status is `unverifiable`, never a guess.
5. ERP access goes through typed tools first, with read-only SQL as an escape hatch.
6. Writes (hold, email, results) happen only in a final gated stage, with a dry-run flag on by default.
7. Documents and emails are untrusted input. The extraction step has no tool access, and its output is validated against a schema.

## 4. Data models

- **Fact:** `id`, `value`, `raw`, `doc`, `location` (page, cell, line or bbox), `method` (text, ocr, vision, erp, email), `confidence`, `as_of`.
- **Requirement (ledger row):** `id`, `scope` (distributor, customer or order), `clause_type`, `params`, `quote` (verbatim), `source` (fact id or doc and location), `source_hash`, `status` (active or superseded), `reviewed`.
- **Finding:** `check_id`, `checklist_ref`, `status` (pass, fail, needs_approval, unverifiable, n/a), `severity`, `compared` (fact ids), `message`, `action`.
- **Order run:** `order`, `revision`, `as_of`, `findings`, `recommendation` (release, hold, needs approval), `state`.

**As-of date.** Cert expiry, quote validity and due dates are judged as of the order date, not the date the code runs.

## 5. Components

**`ingest/`** has one reader per format. Detect an empty text layer and route to vision plus OCR. For identifiers and numbers (accounts, part numbers, quantities, prices), read twice and flag any disagreement with the image crop. Detect locale and validate numbers by `qty x price = extended` and `sum = total`. Extract link annotations. Output is `facts.json` per document with header, lines, notes and links.

**`erp/`** has typed read functions that return facts and encapsulate the traps in section 2. They cover the order and lines, the customer master, the quote, linked and recovered PO lines, inventory and lots, vendors, AR and credit. Batch to one query per table per order. The same functions serve the chatbot.

**`ledger/`** has the closed clause taxonomy, the extractor and the verifiers.
- *Extraction.* Each source is split into units (by headings and numbering). Each unit gets exactly one label: a clause type with params and a verbatim quote, informational, or unclassified. A coverage check requires every unit to be labeled. Long T&Cs are chunked, with the heading path as context and a document-wide pre-pass for definitions. Results are cached per customer and `source_hash`. Run extraction twice with different chunk boundaries and send disagreements to unclassified.
- *Sources of requirements.* Standing: ERP flags (code, no LLM), `ord_notes` (dictionary first, LLM fallback), customer T&Cs. Per order: the PO's own notes and emails. Distributor: our checklist and own rules, such as CoC for unmarked SMT parts and prepay fees.
- *Verifiers.* One function per clause type. Unknown types return `unverifiable`.

**`checks/`** has a registry mapped to checklist item ids (section 6).

**`judge/`** has narrow LLM checks, each with its own prompt. Tools: `get_facts`, `read_source`, `get_requirements`, the ERP lookups, read-only SQL (SELECT only, read-only transaction, row limit), and `record_finding`, which rejects unknown fact ids.

**`report/`** does the rollup and policy, writes JSON and markdown per order, and writes a results table in `worktrial`. `set_order_hold` and `send_email` live here, behind the dry-run flag.

## 6. Check catalogue

Checklist references are to `data/Order_Processing_Checklist.docx`. All checks are code unless marked J (judgment).

**A. Document vs ERP and PO**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| A1 | Header: customer name (strip legal suffixes), PO number, dates, bill-to and ship-to, contacts (§2). |
| A2 | Commercial terms: payment terms, currency, Incoterm, ship via, carrier, account number, partial-shipment policy (§1, §2). |
| A3 | Lines: match on MPN + manufacturer, then compare qty, price, UoM, due date, customer P/N, description. MPN is exact (§2). Duplicate-MPN lines are assigned by qty, price and date. |
| A4 | Arithmetic: line extended, subtotal, total, tax. |
| A5 | Additions and omissions: ack content not requested (allowlist the standard boilerplate), PO content missing from the ack (notes, clauses). J for conflicts with customer clauses. |
| A6 | Ack PDF vs ERP rows (catches a stale or mis-exported ack). |

**B. Customer master and quote**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| B1 | SO terms vs master vs quote vs PO (§1). |
| B2 | Price and cost vs quote (apply the customer's tolerance, for example 2%), quote validity (`valid_days`), quote link recovery (§2). |
| B3 | Credit: limit vs open orders plus AR, for net terms only. Prepay fees (card 3.5%, wire $25) (§1). |
| B4 | Yield flag and required approvals (§3). |
| B5 | Ship account vs `shipinst`, partial instructions vs `no_partials` (§2). |
| B6 | Customer identity resolution: look-alike names exist (Sandstone Lighting C1143 vs Sandstone Electronics Manufacturing C1061, which has the Yield flag). |

**C. Supply**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| C1 | Stock: on hand minus committed, aggregated by item across lines and open orders. Reconcile `itm_inv` against lots and say which we trust (§4). |
| C2 | Inbound: linked and recovered PO lines, due date vs required date. |
| C3 | Lead time: Est Ship vs quoted lead time (regex on `N-M WKS`), and "quoted STOCK but not in stock" (§5). |
| C4 | Unrequested supply: PO lines for parts not on the SO (PO 81797 line 2, PO 81766 line 2). |
| C5 | Cost: SO unit cost vs PO unit cost vs quote cost, and margin. |

**D. Compliance**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| D1 | Country of origin with the hierarchy: PO line `src_cntry`, then allocated lot, then item default (weak), then unknown. Customer prohibitions need approval. The ack must state COO, ECCN and HTS per line when the customer requires it. Quantify China-origin value per order. |
| D2 | Export: destination other than US, or ECCN other than EAR99, requires export review (§6). Flag only. |
| D3 | Date code, shelf life, AS5553/OCM, CoC and similar customer requirements vs our supplier PO conditions and vendor `po_notes`. |
| D4 | Vendor risk: `pay_hold`, ISO expiry as of order date, `po_notes`. |
| D5 | NCNR and T&C conflicts between the ack and the customer's terms. J. |

**E. Ledger verifiers.** The generic mechanism for any clause type (partials, date code, prohibited origin, price tolerance, late-delivery penalty, DFARS/ITAR flow-down, and so on).

**F. Process and document quality**

| Id | Check |
|---|---|
| F1 | Unsigned PO, scan reads that disagree, locale mismatches. |
| F2 | SLA clock, such as "acknowledge within 48 hours". |
| F3 | Referenced but unread terms (links, clause codes like Q2/Q5/Q11, document ids). Always `unverifiable`. |
| F4 | Human-only checklist items (uploads, emailing inspection, test-report approval) are marked as such. |

## 7. LLM policy

Use an LLM only where the problem is "I cannot turn this into canonical form". Never use it to decide whether two identifiers or numbers agree, because disagreement is the finding.

| Step | LLM? |
|---|---|
| Document and clause extraction, email understanding | Primary. |
| Arithmetic, number/date parsing, comparisons, inventory, credit, quote price, origin hierarchy | Never. |
| Manufacturer name to code | Proposal only. Seed from the 14 acks, queue unknowns for review. |
| Payment-terms phrasing | Yes, closed set of 6 term codes, audited. Scope to the terms field. |
| Line matching | Only on ties or lines with no MPN. A near miss is reported as a mismatch with the closest candidate. |
| Incoterms, ship via, account numbers, address, customer name, lead-time text | Code only (regex, alias tables, fuzzy match). |
| Quote or PO link recovery | Code only. A guessed quote would "verify" against the wrong price. |

Fallback tiers: exact, normalized, fuzzy, LLM proposal, unverifiable. LLM output must be a closed set or a cited span. An LLM-resolved value is marked in provenance and cannot produce a pass while the check's other inputs disagree. Approved mappings are cached.

| M4 | Family C | Supply, lead-time and link-recovery issues are caught. |
| M5 | Family D and the ledger verifiers | The origin, export and vendor findings match Appendix A. |
| M6 | Judgment checks and rollup | Each order has a recommendation and a readable summary. |
| M7 | Eval and mutation tests (section 9) | A scored report exists. |
| M8 | Outlook: poll the mailbox, classify, run, reply (to `test@tryrama.com`) | A dropped-in order is processed end to end. |
| M9 | Chatbot reusing the ERP tools | The two example questions in the task answer correctly. |

Written for: you as the builder, and the Rama reviewers who will read the repo.

The plan is in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md). It's a local file, not a shared doc, and I can publish it as a doc if you want to share it. It covers scope, what the data showed, architecture, the check catalogue, build order, evaluation, and a per-order issue list (Appendix A) you can use as an eval answer key. I didn't touch `.gitignore`. Add `.env` and `task.md` there before your first commit, since task.md contains credentials.

## Other problems to solve

The full list of 15 is in section 10. The ones most likely to bite:
- **Revised POs and email handling.** Revisions arrive next to the original, and approvals arrive only by email. None of the sample folders has a revision, so the mailbox needs checking.
- **PO-only mode.** The demo's unseen order may have no SO in the ERP.
- **Approval workflow and customer emails.** Drafting the discrepancy and approval-request emails, and tracking the 24–48 hour clock.
- **Idempotency.** Re-running an order must not duplicate holds or emails.
- **No document storage in the ERP.** Approvals and uploads need your own store, and that's also where a check result gets recorded.
- **Look-alike customers.** Sandstone Lighting and Sandstone Electronics Manufacturing differ in terms and Yield flag, so a wrong match means wrong credit and terms.
- **Unexplored schema.** `customer` has 214 columns and you've seen about 25.

## Gaps in the task doc

- **Model provider.** The only key given is OpenAI, but the doc also says model access comes "on the day". The plan routes all LLM calls through one wrapper so the provider is swappable.
- **"Flags someone."** It doesn't say who or where, and outbound mail only works to `test@tryrama.com`.
- **Checklist inputs not provided.** The Lead Time Matrix, Export Review Form and inspection mailbox are named but not supplied.
- **Supplier-side checks.** Testing and tariffs are mentioned, but no data source is identified.
- **Graph credentials.** They were "sent separately" and aren't in task.md.
- **Empty shipments.** `shp_*` has no rows, though the doc describes shipments.
- **Mailbox vs folder.** The mailbox POs may differ from the folder files.

The full list is in Appendix B for when you're ready to ask.

input.old_string: **`report/`** does the rollup and policy, writes JSON and markdown per order, and writes a results table in `worktrial`. `set_order_hold` and `send_email` live here, behind the dry-run flag.
input.new_string:
**`report/`** does the rollup and policy, writes JSON and markdown per order, and writes a results table in `worktrial`. `set_order_hold` and `send_email` live here, behind the dry-run flag.

**Customer identity.** Resolve the customer first. The ledger and every check hang off it, so a wrong match means wrong terms, credit and requirements. Examples: Sandstone Lighting (C1143, N45) vs Sandstone Electronics Manufacturing (C1061, N30, Yield flag), and Oakridge Imaging (CIA) vs Oakridge Sourcing (N30). In three of the four trial SOs whose terms disagree with the master (Oakridge, Quarry, Crescent), the SO terms equal the look-alike sibling's terms. N30 is also the most common code, so this may be a coincidence, but it is worth testing whether those SOs were keyed from the wrong customer.
- Signals, each stored as a fact: normalized legal name (strip GmbH, K.K., Inc., LLC), bill-to and ship-to street and postcode vs the master, buyer email domain and name vs `contact.b_email` (the two Sandstones use different domains), customer part numbers vs `cust_itm` (to confirm), and PO-number prefix (weak, because siblings share the three-letter prefix).
- Require at least two independent signals to agree, one of them name or address. Otherwise the result is `unverifiable: ambiguous customer` with the candidates listed. Never pick silently.
- Key every lookup on `(cust_no, cust_po)`.

**Storage.** The ERP has no document storage, so we keep four kinds of artifact ourselves:
- *Source documents as received* (pdf, xlsx, jpg, eml, docx), immutable under `store/sources/<sha256>.<ext>`. Provenance locations (page, cell, bbox) only mean something against the exact bytes, so we hash them.
- *Facts*: `store/facts/<sha256>.json`, one per source document.
- *Customer terms (the ledger)*: structured rows in `agent_requirement`, plus the raw source chunks in `agent_source_chunk`, keyed by customer and source hash. A readable per-customer terms document is rendered from the rows for human review. It is a view, not the source of truth.
- *Runs and findings*: `agent_run`, `agent_finding`.

Our tables use the `agent_` prefix in the `worktrial` schema. We do not know whether the database is private to us, so we never touch ERP tables except the gated hold or status write. Approvals and email attachments are stored with the email work.

content.text:
I couldn't read the mailbox, because Microsoft rejects the app ID. I did get the setup done.

**Done:**
- `.env` now holds the Graph and Postgres credentials, using standard `PG*` names so `psql` works from it. It's `chmod 600`.
- `.env` was **not git-ignored**, so I added it to `.gitignore`. There are no commits yet, so nothing leaked. `task.md` is still not ignored, and it contains credentials.
- I added `.env.example` with variable names only.

**What failed:** the token request returned `AADSTS700016`, "application with identifier 202a4b78-… was not found in the directory". The tenant ID is fine: I checked it against `tryrama.com`'s public discovery document and it matches. So the problem is the client ID or the app itself, not the secret. I stopped after one request and didn't try guesses.

**Likely causes:**
- **Wrong ID.** It's easy to copy the Object ID instead of the Application (client) ID. In the Azure portal, open App registrations, then the app, and compare the Overview page's "Application (client) ID" to `202a4b78-…`.
- **Wrong tenant.** The app may be registered in a different tenant and never installed in this one.

If the ID turns out to be right, the next hurdle would be permissions. The app needs admin-consented application permissions such as `Mail.Read` for this to work without a user signing in.

Once you have a corrected client ID, change `GRAPH_CLIENT_ID` in `.env` and tell me. I'll rerun the read-only exploration.

If getting the app fixed is slow, the mailbox login from the task doc works in the browser at outlook.office.com. You could look through it and tell me what you see, though that's slower than the API.

You pasted the client secret into chat, and it's now in this transcript. Since transcripts are a deliverable, rotate that secret after the trial.

S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rama-git-rama-worktrial/4fa92646-869c-4c02-b329-d59b99bad2a1/scratchpad; cd "$S" && python3 - <<'EOF'
import base64, hashlib, json, os, sys, glob
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import graph
D = graph.OUT
# hash every local order doc
local = {}
for f in glob.glob("/Users/rama/git/rama-worktrial/data/order_docs/*/*"):
    local[hashlib.sha256(open(f, "rb").read()).hexdigest()] = f.split("order_docs/")[1]
print("local files hashed:", len(local))

inbox = json.load(open(f"{D}/inbox_preview.json"))
cust = [m for m in inbox if m["receivedDateTime"].startswith("2026-08-31") and (m.get("from") or {}).get("emailAddress", {}).get("address", "").endswith(".example")]
print("customer originals:", len(cust), "\n")
for m in cust:
    frm = m["from"]["emailAddress"]["address"]
    atts = list(graph.get_all(graph.mbox() + f"/messages/{m['id']}/attachments"))
    d = f"{D}/att/customers/{m['id'][-10:]}"; os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    desc = []
    for a in atts:
        raw = base64.b64decode(a.get("contentBytes") or "")
        sha = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        open(f"{d}/{(a['name'] or 'x').replace('/', '_')}", "wb").write(raw)
        desc.append(f"{a['name']} ({a['size']}b, {'inline' if a.get('isInline') else 'file'}) -> " + (("IDENTICAL to " + local[sha]) if sha in local else "NO MATCH in folders"))
    if not atts: desc = ["(no attachment; body only)"]
    print(f"{frm.split('@')[0]:<12} | {(m['subject'] or '')[:34]:<34} | " + " ; ".join(desc))

print("\n== Sent Items: messages that look like our supplier POs")
sent = json.load(open(f"{D}/sentitems_preview.json"))
for m in sent:
    s = m["subject"] or ""
    if "Purchase Order" in s or any(n in s for n in ("81766", "81793", "81797")):
        to = ",".join(r["emailAddress"]["address"] for r in m.get("toRecipients", []))
        atts = list(graph.get_all(graph.mbox() + f"/messages/{m['id']}/attachments")) if m["hasAttachments"] else []
        desc = []
        for a in atts:
            raw = base64.b64decode(a.get("contentBytes") or "")
            sha = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
            desc.append(f"{a['name']} -> " + (("IDENTICAL to " + local[sha]) if sha in local else "no match"))
        print(m["sentDateTime"][:16], "to", to[:36], "|", s[:40], "|", "; ".join(desc) or "no attachment")
EOF

**`intake/`** (stage 0) decides whether a message is a customer PO before anything else runs.
- *Scope.* Inbox only. Sent Items is read only to fetch our supplier POs on demand. Drafts and Deleted Items are ignored. We never move, delete or mark mail read. State lives in our own table `agent_message` (message id, internet message id, label, reasons, run id, processed time), not in Outlook categories, because the mailbox is shared and other candidates would see them.
- *Labels (closed set).* `customer_po` and `po_revision` run the pipeline (no revision example exists yet). `order_reply` is logged and not acted on yet. `rfq`, `supplier_correspondence`, `agent_output` (replies written by any agent, ours or others'), `automated_notice` (Vanta, GoDaddy and similar), `other_candidate_test` and `other` are ignored. `unsure` goes to a human queue and never runs.
- *Layers.*
  1. Deterministic metadata filters: skip mail sent by the mailbox itself, known automated senders and subject prefixes (`[Order agent]`, `[Order desk agent]`, `[B]`, `RFQ ingested`), and an editable ignore list (gmail.com for now, since other candidates test from gmail).
  2. Content signals on what remains: attachment types and names, PO-number pattern, body text, language.
  3. An LLM classifier for what the rules cannot settle, with structured output: closed label, reasons and confidence. Below the threshold the label is `unsure`.
  4. Per-attachment role: `po`, `terms` or `other`. Inline images such as signatures are ignored.
  5. Ingest then re-checks that the document is a PO addressed to Demo Distributor, with a PO number, lines and totals, and stops if it is not (check F5).
- *Sender is a signal, not a gate.* The demo order may not come from a `.example` address. Unknown senders are classified on content. A PO whose customer cannot be resolved is flagged, not processed. A manual override (`--message-id`) forces any message through.
- *Idempotency.* Key on `internetMessageId`, attachment SHA-256 and `(cust_no, cust_po)`. A byte-identical resend (for example another candidate's copy of Meridian's PO) is skipped as a duplicate.
- *Modes.* `replay` takes an explicit list of message ids (the 14 originals, and evaluation). `watch` polls the Inbox with a Graph delta query from a start-time watermark, so the 405 historical messages are never processed. Delta with the app's permissions needs confirming.
- *Outbound policy.* Replies go only to `test@tryrama.com`, never to the sender. Customer addresses bounce and gmail senders are other candidates. Dry-run by default.

content.text:
Triage is now stage 0 in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md), under a new `intake/` component. The pipeline runs only on messages labeled as customer POs, and ingest re-checks and stops if a document isn't a PO.

## Why simple rules won't work

I measured them on the 405 Inbox messages, against the 14 real POs:

| Rule | Real POs caught | False positives |
|---|---|---|
| Subject has a PO number | 10 of 14 | 59 |
| Has an attachment | 13 of 14 | 95 |
| Sender isn't tryrama.com or gmail.com | 14 of 14 | 90 |
| Metadata and content rules combined | 14 of 14 | 22 |

The PO-number rule misses four real POs (subjects like "PO", "order", "PO for quote 20261299", "Ironclad PO attached"). Its false positives are other agents' replies, which put PO numbers in their subjects, and gmail test emails. Combined rules narrow 405 messages to 36 candidates, so the LLM only has to reject about 22.

## Decisions we can make now

1. **Scope.** Triage reads the Inbox only. Sent Items is read only to fetch our supplier POs on demand. Drafts and Deleted Items are ignored.
2. **Labels.** A closed set. `customer_po` and `po_revision` run the pipeline. Everything else is ignored: replies from any agent, automated notices, RFQs, other candidates' tests. `unsure` goes to a human queue and never runs.

## 5. Components

**`intake/`** (stage 0) decides whether a message is a customer PO before anything else runs.
- *Scope.* Inbox only. Sent Items is read only to fetch our supplier POs on demand. Drafts and Deleted Items are ignored. We never move, delete or mark mail read. State lives in our own table `agent_message` (message id, internet message id, label, reasons, run id, processed time), not in Outlook categories, because the mailbox is shared and other candidates would see them.
- *Labels (closed set).* `customer_po` and `po_revision` run the pipeline (no revision example exists yet). `order_reply` is logged and not acted on yet. `rfq`, `supplier_correspondence`, `agent_output` (replies written by any agent, ours or others'), `automated_notice` (Vanta, GoDaddy and similar), `other_candidate_test` and `other` are ignored. `unsure` goes to a human queue and never runs.
- *Layers.*
  1. Deterministic metadata filters: skip mail sent by the mailbox itself, known automated senders and subject prefixes (`[Order agent]`, `[Order desk agent]`, `[B]`, `RFQ ingested`), and an editable ignore list (gmail.com for now, since other candidates test from gmail).
  2. Content signals on what remains: attachment types and names, PO-number pattern, body text, language.
  3. An LLM classifier for what the rules cannot settle, with structured output: closed label, reasons and confidence. Below the threshold the label is `unsure`.
  4. Per-attachment role: `po`, `terms` or `other`. Inline images such as signatures are ignored.
  5. Ingest then re-checks that the document is a PO addressed to Demo Distributor, with a PO number, lines and totals, and stops if it is not (check F5).
- *Sender is a signal, not a gate.* The demo order may not come from a `.example` address. Unknown senders are classified on content. A PO whose customer cannot be resolved is flagged, not processed. A manual override (`--message-id`) forces any message through.
- *Idempotency.* Key on `internetMessageId`, attachment SHA-256 and `(cust_no, cust_po)`. A byte-identical resend (for example another candidate's copy of Meridian's PO) is skipped as a duplicate.
- *Modes.* `replay` takes an explicit list of message ids (the 14 originals, and evaluation). `watch` polls the Inbox with a Graph delta query from a start-time watermark, so the 405 historical messages are never processed. Delta with the app's permissions needs confirming.
- *Outbound policy.* Replies go only to `test@tryrama.com`, never to the sender. Customer addresses bounce and gmail senders are other candidates. Dry-run by default.

Not handled yet, and labeled `unsure`: zip files, links to a customer portal, password-protected files.

Only `customer_po` and `po_revision` continue to ingest.

The triage design is now in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md): one sender gate, and everything else goes to the classifier.

**Sender gate.** Mail from `test@tryrama.com` itself is ignored without a classifier call. That covers our own replies and the other candidates' agents, who also send from the shared mailbox. It's 151 of the 405 Inbox messages, and it's the main loop guard. I kept the `X-Order-Agent` header on our outgoing mail as a second layer. The known cost: a demo order sent from `test@tryrama.com` itself would be ignored.

**Everything else gets the classifier call.** The label is `customer_po`, `po_revision`, `not_po` or `unsure`, and no other sender, domain or subject gates it.

**Every form of PO is handled.** The classifier reads the email body and each attachment. That means text PDFs, scanned PDFs, images, xlsx, docx, a forwarded `.eml`, and a PO typed into the body like Sandstone's. Each attachment is reduced to a snippet, using a text extract or the image itself for scans and photos. Zips, portal links and password-protected files are labeled `unsure`.

**Recall over precision.** `unsure` still goes through the ingest gate, which stops anything that isn't a PO addressed to Demo Distributor. A missed order costs more than a wasted run.

**Revisions come after the call.** Once the customer is resolved, an identical file is skipped as a duplicate. The same customer and PO number with different content is treated as a revision, even if the classifier said `customer_po`.

**Replies.** They go to `test@tryrama.com` only, as a new message carrying the original subject plus the PO and SO, and dry-run is the default.

**Other candidates.** Their mail is handled through classification, dedupe, and a short exact-address suppress list (the two gmail addresses seen so far), with no domain-level rules.

1. **The PO itself.** Most of the findings are PO vs SO differences, not terms: Copperfield's quantity and freight account, Cobalt's price, Ospreyfield's part number. So the agent has to extract the customer's PO from the email (PDF, scan, image, xlsx, docx or body) and compare it line by line with the SO.

Here's how I'd build both. Extraction is mostly code plus one structured LLM call per document. Running the checklist is a registry of checks driven by code.

## Extracting the PO (and the ack, the same way)

1. **Normalize each format into page text and/or images, in code:**
   - Text PDF: PyMuPDF gives words with positions, the page image, and link annotations. The T&C URLs live in the annotations.
   - Scanned PDF or image: no text layer, so render the page image.
   - xlsx: openpyxl, dumped as cells with their refs (`B5 = Net 30`). Keep values as strings so part numbers like `064316` keep their leading zeros.
   - docx: python-docx, paragraphs plus table cells.
   - Email body: from Graph, repairing quoted-printable breaks like `10/18=` + newline + `/2026`.
2. **One LLM call per document, with structured output.** It gets the text and the page image together. It fills a fixed schema and copies each value **verbatim, as printed**, with its location. It does no parsing or normalization.
   ```
   header: po_number, po_date, customer_name, buyer{name,email}, bill_to, ship_to,
           payment_terms, incoterm, ship_via, carrier_account, currency,
           notes[], tc_refs[], links[]
   lines[]: line_no, customer_pn, mpn, manufacturer, description,
            qty, uom, unit_price, extended, required_date
   totals: subtotal, tax, total
   every field = { raw: "000158830", loc: {page: 1, region|cell|line} }
   ```
3. **Code parses and validates the raw strings.**
   - **Numbers and dates:** parse locale-aware, then pick the reading where qty × price = extended and the lines sum to the total. That's how Oakridge's `19.000` resolves.
   - **Part numbers:** stay exact strings.
   - **Manufacturers:** map names to ERP codes through an alias table.
   - **Is-a-PO gate:** stop unless the document is addressed to Demo Distributor and has a PO number and lines.
4. **Grounding checks.**
   - Text sources: every `raw` value must appear in the source text. This catches the model inventing or "correcting" a value.
   - Scans and images: a second independent read (Tesseract OCR) on part numbers, quantities, prices and account numbers. Any disagreement is flagged with the image crop.
5. **One retry with feedback** ("line 2 doesn't tie out, re-read"). If it still fails, those fields are marked uncertain, not guessed.

The ack and supplier POs use the same schema plus a few fields: ship option, shipping terms, freight account, est ship. Long conditions pages, like Quarry's page 2, go to the terms extraction, not this call.

## Running the checklist items

1. **Build an order bundle once.** It holds:
   - the PO and ack facts;
   - the ERP SO and lines;
   - the customer master;
   - the quote;
   - linked and recovered supplier PO lines;
   - inventory and lots;
   - vendor flags;
   - AR and open orders;
   - the customer's terms ledger.
2. **Match lines in code.** Each line is paired across PO, SO, ack, quote and supply on MPN plus manufacturer. Lines with the same MPN (Norwood, Granite Peak) are paired on qty, price and date.
3. **Keep a registry of checks in code.** Each check has an id, the checklist item it serves, the inputs it needs, and a function that returns findings. Every check runs on every order, in a fixed order. A missing input gives `unverifiable`.
   - *Comparisons:* terms, partials, account, lines, totals, credit, Yield flag, stock, lead time, origin.
   - *Terms-ledger verifiers:* one per clause type. For example, `prohibited_origin` runs the origin hierarchy per line.
   - *A few LLM judgment checks:* T&C conflicts, clauses no verifier recognizes, and the summary. They must cite facts, and they can't overturn a code result.
   - *Human-only items:* uploads and the inspection email, marked as manual.
4. **Roll up to Demo's checklist.** Each of the roughly 25 items in the checklist docx maps to check ids, and the worst status wins: fail, then needs approval, then unverifiable, then pass. A policy table turns that into release, hold or needs approval.

§2 Line 3 quantity      PASS   9,300 (PO p1 line 3) = 9,300 (ord_detl 503097/3)

Mostly yes, with one correction: the order bundle isn't the checklist. The bundle is the evidence, the checklist is the questions, and the findings are the answers.

- **Email and attachments → JSON.** Yes. The PO, whether it's a PDF, scan, image, xlsx, docx or the email body, becomes `facts.json`.

- **Checklist.** Demo's order checklist plus the clauses from the customer's terms ledger. Each item is a check that runs over the bundle and returns pass, fail, needs approval or unverifiable, citing the facts it compared.

I've added the extraction steps, the check runner, and an "order bundle" entry to the data models in section 5 of [PLAN.md](PLAN.md). The Meridian example output is under `checks/`.

content.text:
Close, but the bundle is built by plain code, not by an LLM agent. Going through the checklist is mostly code too. The LLM is used at specific steps, not as a free-roaming agent.

| Step | Who does it |
|---|---|
| 1. Triage the email (is it a PO?) | LLM, one call |
| 2. Extract the PO and ack into JSON | LLM, one call per document, then code validates |
| 3. Load the SO, quote, inventory, lots, supplier POs, vendors, credit | Code, fixed queries keyed by customer and PO number |
| 4. Build or refresh the customer's terms ledger | LLM, cached per customer |
| 5. Assemble the bundle and match lines | Code |
| 6. Run the checklist | Code registry, with LLM only for a few judgment checks (T&C conflicts, unrecognized clauses) |
| 7. Roll up and decide release, hold or needs approval | Code |
| 8. Write the reply summarizing the problems | LLM writes the text from the findings, code sends it to `test@tryrama.com` |

So "the agent" is the whole pipeline, and the LLM does what code can't: read messy documents, interpret clauses, make judgment calls, write prose. I'm keeping code in charge of the rest for three reasons:
- **Every check always runs.** An LLM walking a checklist can skip items or stop early.
- **Mismatches survive.** An LLM tends to explain away 000158830 vs 000158380 as "the same account". Code just says they differ.
- **Same input, same result.** That makes the eval and the demo reproducible.

The two places where a tool-using agent fits are the judgment checks (read-only ERP tools, must cite facts) and the chatbot.

I noted in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) that the bundle is built in code with no LLM.
